notes: PSA 9.2 ng/mL. PI-RADS 4. PSAD 0.17. Prostate volume 53 mL. DRE nodus. csPCa 0.79.

note_sections.t: Re-evaluation for rising PSA to 9.2 ng/mL despite a prior negative biopsy and a new PI-RADS 4 lesion on MRI.

Long-standing referral for monitoring of prostate-specific antigen levels. The patient is a 57-year-old retired shopkeeper, recently relocated to live with his sister. He reports mild lower urinary tract symptoms, with an IPSS score of 5, managed with tamsulosin. He is an ex-smoker, having quit in 2003, and is currently alcohol-free. He walks 20 minutes daily. Recent appointments include a vascular surgery consult for varicose veins, an orthopaedic follow-up for his knee, and six sessions of physiotherapy for lower back pain. His nephew acts as his next of kin. The PSA has risen progressively from 2.1 ng/mL in November 2022 to 9.2 ng/mL in January 2025. A previous biopsy was negative.
On digital rectal examination, a nodule is palpated, consistent with clinical stage cT2a. General examination is unremarkable, with normal vital signs and no lymphadenopathy.
